items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the correction law, in relation to allowing a telephone call
prior to an inmate's transfer
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S402

SPONSOR: BIAGGI
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the correction law, in relation to allowing a telephone
call prior to an inmate's transfer

 
PURPOSE:

To provide that state inmates transferred to a new correctional facility
are able to call their families prior to being transferred and the
department will send an electronic notice to the next of kin or personal
representative.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends subdivision 1 of section 23 of the correction law.

Section 2 provides an effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Inmates are routinely transferred from one facility to another for a
variety of reasons. Immediately before transfer they are locked down for
a few days, then are sent by bus to their new facility. The bus may take
several days to arrive at the new facility, since it usually makes other
stops along the way. Once an inmate reaches a new facility, they are
initially placed in special housing and then eventually transferred to
general population.

Unfortunately, many family members and loved ones take trips and spend
money in order visit the inmate, just to be turned away upon arrival
because their loved one has been transferred to a new facility. DOCCS
does not tell family members when an inmate is being transferred and
since the inmates are locked down, they cannot phone home. Allowing an
inmate to call home prior to being transferred can help relieve the
stress that inmates and their families feel around the time of transfer
and can make the transition to a new prison easier. Family members can
avoid the financial burden of visiting the wrong facility and/or sending
packages that may become lost in the mail. The electronic notice ensures
that the next of kin or personal representative is notified in case they
missed the call.

This bill follows current DOCCS practice of allowing an inmate to phone
home once the transfer is completed but expands that practice by permit-
ting inmates to call their loved ones immediately prior to being trans-
ferred too.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: S3100, died on third reading; A6867, died in correction, died
on third reading

2018: S8966A, died in rules; A10829B, died on third reading

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day after it shall have
become a law

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 121
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 402-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the correction law, in relation to allowing a tele-
      phone call prior to an incarcerated individual's transfer"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would  require the Department of Corrections and Community
Services (DOCCS) to electronically notify an  incarcerated  individual's
next  of  kin or personal representative immediately before transferring
the individual to another facility.  DOCCS  currently  facilitates  more
than  25,000  transfers per year, most often in 20- and 40-person buses,
through a centralized transportation system. To keep incarcerated  indi-
viduals and DOCCS staff safe, DOCCS does not currently disclose when and
where  an incarcerated individual is to be transferred immediately prior
to the transfer.
 
  I recognize the importance of allowing an incarcerated individual  the
ability to notify their loved ones when they are moved to another facil-
ity.  However,  enacting  this law will create unacceptable risks to the
safety of incarcerated individuals and Department staff.
 
  Therefore, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
